                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-14.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">14</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q14.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> With regards to the outcomes and experiences of Erasmus+ activities</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are monitored, evaluated and disseminated as a way to improve international cooperation and mobility activities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Linked with the overall internationalisation strategy of the institution, monitoring and evaluation of cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility is essential if HEIs are to learn from their experiences. Monitoring and evaluation is more than just measuring the number and types of outputs, it needs to include capturing information on the overall outcomes and experiences of the activities at the institutional and the individual level. Systematic monitoring and evaluation should therefore include more qualitative approaches, which expressly capture the experiences in a way which helps the institution to understand the added value of its involvement in these activities. Documenting and analysing the outcomes and experiences is only the first step. To learn from the approaches taken, and the benefits gained, institutions should take time to disseminate the findings of the cooperation projects and mobility periods through, for example, meetings, workshops and publications, social media, etc. These activities will embed good practice, help the institution to iteratively improve its approach and also feed back into the on-going monitoring and evaluation.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are used systematically for the benefit of your institution, providing internationalisation at home, hence enhancing intercultural competences of non-mobile students and staff</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The outcomes and experiences of cooperation and Erasmus+ mobility have a much wider impact than just improving mobile activities. All institutions have significant numbers of non-mobile staff and students who can benefit from the international experiences of others. As part of the monitoring and evaluation processes, HEIs should consider the impact which can be specifically made on non-mobile staff and students, giving them “internationalisation at home experiences”. This includes building international competences, cultural awareness, virtual mobility opportunities, inviting international lecturers and embedding student projects with an international focus into the curricula, and providing opportunities for local students to work together with incoming mobile participants in e.g. project work, to ensure that local students benefit from the presence of mobile students at their institution. This fits with the activities of disseminating the overall outcomes and experiences of the cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility, though tailored to a different audience. It should take into account the professional development needs of the staff at the HEI and the perspectives of non-mobile students.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are exploited and disseminated, by providing participants with the results of cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility opportunities (e.g. presentations) to share funding possibilities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The dissemination of outcomes is an integral part of mobility projects. Good practice would be to ensure that the dissemination is built into the support measure and participants in projects and mobility actions are allocated adequate time, resources and space to disseminate their experiences and exploit project results. This includes opportunities to share new knowledge and to highlight new opportunities (including funding) which have arisen from the new relationships formed. In order to do this, HEIs should provide support functions such as web platforms to collect results or opportunities to present results at the institutional or departmental level, as relevant.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">After the mobility Erasmus+ participants have the opportunity to present their newly acquired competences</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The study entitled ‘Effects of mobility on the skills and employability of students and the internationalisation of higher education institutions’ showcases how mobility can contribute to the internationalisation of higher education institutions, including the impacts on teaching methods, cooperation between HEIs and perception of staff more generally. Therefore the dissemination of outcomes is an integral part of mobility projects. Good practice would be to ensure that the dissemination is built into the support measure and participants in projects and mobility actions are allocated adequate time, resources and space to disseminate their experiences and exploit project results. This includes opportunities to share new knowledge and to highlight new opportunities (including funding) which have arisen from the new relationships formed. In order to do this, HEIs should provide support functions such as web platforms to collect results or opportunities to present results at the institutional or departmental level, as relevant.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/capitalising-on-the-outcomes-and-experiences-of-erasmus-activities" target="_blank">Capitalising on the outcomes and experiences of Erasmus+ activities</a></div>

                                             </div>

Job Description is only in German, as the Job requires proficiency in German language.

Klub44 ist ein gemeinnütziges Startup im Bereich digitale Jugendbeteiligung. Mit der Klub-App ermöglichen wir es jungen Menschen, ihre eigene Stadt und ihre Vorlieben zu entdecken, und die Welt um sich herum mitzugestalten. Alle jungen Menschen haben das Recht auf ein freies und schöpferisches Leben, daran glauben wir fest.

Nebenbei möchten wir die Schul- und Berufsbildung radikal transformieren.

Mit der Klub-App erhalten Jugendliche ab 12 Jahren einen chancengerechten Zugang zu kostenfreien Freizeit- und Berufsorientierungsangeboten. Außerschulische Standorte – z. B. Jugendclubs, Makerspaces, Orte der kulturellen Bildung – können auf unserer App ihre Angebote direkt und digital an Jugendliche kommunizieren. Das Ganze bauen wir als Game auf: Entdecke deine Stadt, dich selbst, und bekomme dafür Rewards!

Wir ermutigen ausdrücklich Menschen aller Geschlechter, Religionen und sexuellen Orientierungen dazu, sich bei uns zu bewerben!

Aufgaben

Als Projektmanager*in Kooperationen bist du die Person, bei der unsere operativen Projekte zusammenlaufen. Kommunen, Schulen und Stiftungen arbeiten mit uns, weil sie ein Ergebnis wollen – du sorgst dafür, dass dieses Ergebnis auch eintritt: im Zeitplan, im Budget, und mit zufriedenen Partnern. Gleichzeitig hast du einen zweiten Auftrag, der genauso wichtig ist: Du führst so viele Projekte wie möglich über unsere Standardprozesse, damit Klub als Plattform skalierbar bleibt und nicht in Sonderlösungen erstickt. Diese Doppelrolle – nach außen verbindlich, nach innen konsequent – ist der Kern des Jobs.

Wir freuen uns auf Mitunternehmer*innen, um gemeinsam mit dem jungen Team und Geschäftsführer Sebastian die Geschicke von Klub44 zu leiten.

Projektsteuerung

  • Eigenverantwortliche Steuerung unserer laufenden Kooperationsprojekte – von Kick-off bis Abschluss.
  • Planung von Meilensteinen, Verantwortlichkeiten und Terminen; Nachhalten, wenn es hakt.
  • Frühzeitiges Erkennen von Risiken und aktives Gegensteuern, statt Überraschungen am Projektende.
  • Sicherstellen, dass zugesagte Ziele (z. B. teilnehmende Standorte, aktive Jugendliche, Angebots-Uploads) tatsächlich erreicht werden.

Account Management & Partnerbetreuung

  • Du bist die verlässliche Ansprechperson für unsere Projektpartner in Kommunen, Schulen und Stiftungen – die Stimme von Klub im Alltag.
  • Aufbau langfristiger Beziehungen: Bestehende Kooperationen erfolgreich umsetzen, verlängern und ausbauen.
  • Erwartungsmanagement mit Verwaltungen, Schulleitungen und Förderpartnern: klar sagen, was geht, und was nicht.
  • Übersetzungsarbeit zwischen kommunaler Logik und Startup-Tempo – in beide Richtungen.

Skalierbarkeit & Standardprozesse

  • Onboarding von Kommunen, Schulen und Jugendeinrichtungen entlang unserer Standardprozesse – wiederholbar statt jedes Mal neu.
  • Weiterentwicklung dieser Prozesse: Playbooks, Templates, Checklisten, Automatisierungen.
  • Erkennen, wann eine Partneranfrage ein Sonderfall ist – und wann sie in ein neues Standardangebot gehört.
  • Bewusstes Nein zu Individuallösungen, die uns langfristig teuer werden.

Zahlen, Reporting & Wirkung

  • Nachhalten der Projekt-KPIs und transparentes internes Reporting zum Projektstatus.
  • Aufbereitung von Projektständen und Wirkungsdaten für Zuwendungsgeber und Stiftungen – die Verantwortung für Verwendungsnachweise und Reportings liegt bei der Geschäftsführung, du lieferst die Grundlage.
  • Ableiten konkreter Maßnahmen aus den Zahlen, nicht nur Dokumentation.

Zusammenarbeit im Team

  • Enge Abstimmung mit Geschäftsführung, Marketing & Community und Produktentwicklung.
  • Rückkopplung von Partner-Feedback ins Produkt: Was brauchen Kommunen und Standorte wirklich?
  • Steuerung externer Partner und Dienstleister im Projektkontext.

Qualifikation

  • Du hast mehrjährige Erfahrung im Projektmanagement und bringst Projekte nachweislich zum Abschluss – idealerweise mit Partnern aus Verwaltung, Bildung, Stiftungen oder NGOs. Arbeitserfahrung in einem Startup ist ein guter Bonus.
  • Du bist stark in Kooperation und Kommunikation: Du gewinnst Menschen für gemeinsame Ziele und behältst dabei die Interessen von Klub im Blick.
  • Du denkst in Prozessen und Systemen, nicht in Einzelfällen – und hast Freude daran, Wiederholbares zu bauen.
  • Du arbeitest strukturiert und verbindlich: Zusagen, Fristen und Follow-ups sitzen bei dir.
  • Du bist "hands on" und sicher im Umgang mit agilen Methoden und Projektmanagement-Tools.
  • Du arbeitest datenbasiert und bist sicher im Nachhalten von Kennzahlen.
  • Dich motivieren unternehmerische Herausforderungen und du möchtest persönlich dazu beitragen, Jugendliche bei einer chancengerechten Entfaltung ihrer Potenziale zu fördern.
  • Du hast sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse auf muttersprachlichem Niveau und verhandlungssichere Englischkenntnisse.

Benefits

Als junges, gemeinnütziges Startup sind wir noch limitiert, wollen aber mittelfristig marktgerecht zahlen. Bis wir das hinkriegen, können wir auch kreativ sein.

Zur Orientierung:

  • Jahresgrundgehalt je nach Erfahrung €38 – 45.000
  • 80% Arbeitszeit unter Umständen möglich
  • Hybrides Arbeiten (3 Tage Office, 2 Tage Home ist unser Standard)
  • 28 Urlaubstage

Wir wollen die Rolle so schnell wie möglich besetzen.

Unsere Werte zur gemeinsamen Zusammenarbeit nach innen und außen sind:

  • Liebevoll
  • Aktivierend
  • Verbunden
  • Spielerisch
  • Ehrlich

Einsatzort: Erlangen

Sie verfügen über fundierte Erfahrung im Risikomanagement internationaler EPC- oder Turnkey-Großprojekte und kennen die Herausforderungen komplexer Projektabwicklungen im Anlagenbau? Als Project Risk Manager (m/w/d) sorgen Sie dafür, dass Risiken und Chancen frühzeitig erkannt, transparent bewertet und während der gesamten Projektabwicklung aktiv gesteuert werden. Dabei arbeiten Sie eng mit Projektleitung und Projektteam zusammen, koordinieren geeignete Maßnahmen und schaffen belastbare Entscheidungsgrundlagen für eine erfolgreiche Projektabwicklung.

  • Steuerung der Risiken und Chancen in komplexen internationalen EPC- und Turnkey-Projekten
  • Identifikation und Bewertung technischer, kommerzieller, terminlicher und vertraglicher Projektrisiken und -chancen
  • Entwicklung, Abstimmung und Nachverfolgung geeigneter Maßnahmen zur Risikominimierung und Chancennutzung
  • Durchführung und Moderation von Risk Reviews und Workshops mit Projektleitung, Fachbereichen und weiteren Projektstakeholdern
  • Anwendung und konsequente Umsetzung etablierter Risikomanagement-Prozesse und -Methoden innerhalb der Projektabwicklung
  • Sicherstellung einer transparenten, nachvollziehbaren und auditierbaren Risiko- und Chancendokumentation sowie entsprechendes Reporting

Qualifikation

Hi, we're Dana and Erik, the founders of Circonomit. We build the decision platform industrial companies use to plan their production.

Dana sees the customer side. She needs to know which use cases we can sell today, which we cannot, and what a demo is allowed to claim.

Erik sees the engineering side. He needs requirements that are ready to be built, complete, and clear about what we deliberately leave out.

The product sits between the two, and that is this role. We sell vertically, one use case at a time, while the product has to stay general enough to serve the next customer without being rebuilt. You decide what we build next, in which order, and what we decline.

How you will be measured: how much of today's project work is standard product a year from now, and how quickly a recognised customer problem becomes a usable capability.

We came out of RWTH research, raised €2.8M with Vorwerk Ventures, and have customers running on our models today. Small team, Cologne office.

Requirements

  • 5+ years in product management, or consulting with genuine product proximity. You have owned a product area end to end, not only a backlog.
  • A technical and analytical foundation: engineering, data, operations research, quantitative controlling, or finance with real modelling.
  • You recognise when a requirement creates technical debt or will not be reusable at the next customer. You will not write production code.
  • Experience deciding under incomplete information, and explaining the trade-offs afterwards: what you chose, why, and what it cost.
  • You are comfortable working directly with plant managers and controllers, and understand how they decide today.
  • German at C1 level or above, and fluent English. Customer conversations happen in German.
  • Existing work visa for Germany.

You should enjoy being in front of customers in your first week, and deciding without a research team behind you. Priorities change as we learn from customers, and we make scope and trade-offs explicit together.

Benefits

  • Ownership. The roadmap, and where the line between product and customer project sits.
  • Shaping the role. This is the founding product role. You define how product works here: discovery, prioritisation, and the standards between product and engineering.
  • Exposure. You present your roadmap and the reasoning behind it to the board, and you sit in the core strategy conversations.
  • Real-world impact. Customers plan their production on our models today.
  • Direct collaboration. Small team, no org chart. We work directly together. Weekly feedback, both ways.
  • Compensation. Competitive salary plus a VSOP package reflecting your contribution and development in the role.
  • Hybrid work. Our HQ is in Cologne, and we meet there regularly.
  • Your setup and everyday extras. Hardware of your choice · AI tooling budget · sports membership · Deutschland-Ticket.

Process: An intro call, a second conversation with the team, a 60- to 90-minute live case on a real customer requirement, then in-person conversations with the team.

"Hustle the day, analyse at night, reinforce something outstanding." Period.

  • Work directly with semiconductor foundries and process engineers, providing clear, actionable feedback that can be used to improve device performance, consistency and yield.

  • Build scalable characterisation processes, establishing testing standards, calibration procedures, SOPs and data pipelines that allow information to flow effectively between semiconductor process integration and quantum engineering teams.

  • Help shape how we characterise the next generation of our technology, bringing your expertise and ideas to continuously improve our measurement capability as Quantum Motion scales.

  • We are looking for someone who combines strong semiconductor device knowledge with a practical, data-driven approach to electrical characterisation.

  • Master's or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Microelectronics, Semiconductor Physics, Materials Science or a closely related discipline.

  • 3+ years' experience in semiconductor device testing, reliability engineering, electrical characterisation or yield analysis within a foundry, IDM or semiconductor R&D environment.

  • Strong understanding of silicon CMOS fabrication processes, semiconductor device physics and foundry workflows.

  • Strong Python skills, particularly for instrument control, automation and automated test execution.

At Statista, we’re all about facts and data, for we are the world's leading business data platform. By providing reliable and easy-to-use data as well as various data analytics products and services, we empower people worldwide to make fact-based decisions.

Founded in Hamburg in 2007, we have quickly grown into a global company with offices in major cities such as London, New York, Berlin and Tokyo. And we still have a lot of plans. Our constant growth does not only prove our success, but also keeps creating new development and career opportunities for our employees.

We value and celebrate our diverse culture. You are welcome here for who you are, no matter where you come from, what you look like, or whether you prefer bar graphs to pie charts. Your story matters – keep writing it as part of our team.

Are you ready to join us?

What you will own:

Strategic Account Development

  • Own a portfolio of enterprise accounts with ACV in the £50k–£300k+ range — and the mandate to grow them.

  • Build and maintain a live account plan for every account in your portfolio: org map, stakeholder matrix, expansion roadmap, commercial milestones, and renewal forecast.

  • Move relationships up the decision-maker hierarchy — from research and insights teams to VP, Director, and C-suite economic buyers.

  • Develop the institutional depth that makes Statista’s position in each account structurally difficult to challenge: multiple threads, multiple use cases, multiple stakeholders.

Drive the Enterprise Commercial Motion

  • Run structured, consultative discovery conversations that surface the business problems Statista solves — not product pitches that describe features.

  • Build and present business cases and ROI frameworks at executive level that justify six-figure commercial commitments.

  • Navigate complex multi-stakeholder enterprise cycles — champion, technical buyer, economic buyer, procurement, legal — with discipline and patience.

  • Lead Connect expansion conversations in your accounts — identifying where Statista data is being retrieved manually and positioning Connect’s consumption-based model as the infrastructure replacement.

  • Open Statista+ conversations where accounts are using Statista data to brief decisions — positioning the analytical layer as a natural next step.

Protect GRR and Drive NRR

  • Own renewal outcomes for every account in your portfolio. Renewals are the floor. Expansion is the ceiling.

  • Monitor and act on usage signals, stakeholder changes, and risk indicators before they become churn conversations.

  • Run high-quality QBRs that demonstrate ROI, deepen relationships, and create the commercial conversations that expansion depends on.

  • Partner with the CSM aligned to your accounts to ensure adoption, value realisation, and renewal are a joined-up motion.

Represent Statista in the Market

  • Operate as a credible commercial partner at VP and C-suite level — the person clients call when they are making strategic data and intelligence decisions, not just when they need to renew a licence.

  • Champion the full OneStatista platform — core, Connect, Statista+, and the StatistaIQ roadmap — in every enterprise engagement.

  • Contribute account intelligence to the commercial planning process — where are the opportunities, where are the risks, what is the market telling us?

What we are looking for:

Essential

  • Significant B2B enterprise account management experience with a track record of protecting and growing strategic accounts at £100k+ ACV.

  • Proven ability to move relationships from operational contacts to economic buyers — and to run commercial conversations at VP and C-suite level.

  • Evidence of running complex, multi-stakeholder enterprise cycles with rigour and discipline — not just renewing what exists.

  • Strong consultative and discovery skills — you can run a client conversation that uncovers problems the client hasn’t articulated yet, and build a business case that justifies the investment.

  • Commercial instinct for expansion — you see whitespace, surface latent needs, and progress expansion conversations with the same discipline as new business.

  • Self-directed and ownership-minded — you run your accounts with the commercial rigour of a business owner, not the activity of a relationship manager.

Desirable

  • Experience in data, intelligence, research, information services, or AI-adjacent platforms.

  • Familiarity with consumption-based or API-led commercial models.

  • Exposure to enterprise procurement, compliance, and risk conversations in regulated industries (financial services, consulting, healthcare, technology).

  • Experience working across multiple European markets.

  • Fluency in a European language (French, German, Dutch) is advantageous.

    About the Role:

    Hi there! We're hiring a Senior Product Marketing Manager to join our Product Marketing team.

    We're a group that cares about getting the story right, not just getting it out the door. We work closely with product, sales, and demand gen, and we hold ourselves to a high bar because our work directly shapes how the market understands what we build.

    This role gives you real ownership. You'll shape positioning and messaging for a meaningful piece of our product portfolio, build the competitive intelligence that keeps our field teams sharp, and work directly with sales leaders who depend on your materials to close deals. It's a role with visible impact, not one where your work disappears into a shared drive.

    As a Senior Product Marketing Manager, you'll drive go-to-market strategy for your area, from positioning through launch through enablement, while partnering with product and sales to make sure the message actually lands. This role matters because clear, credible product marketing is what turns a strong platform into a business result. Camunda operates in a technical, complex space, and getting that translation right is not optional.

    What You Will Do

    • Own positioning and messaging for your product area, translating technical capability into a clear value proposition for both technical and business buyers.

    • Build and maintain a competitive intelligence program that sales actually uses, not just battlecards that sit in a folder.

    • Lead go-to-market execution for launches in your area, coordinating across product, sales, and demand gen so the message is consistent everywhere it shows up.

    • Arm the field with content that works in real conversations: pitch decks, demos, solution briefs, and objection handling.

    • Use market and customer research to inform product and positioning decisions, not just to validate ones already made.

    • Mentor and support other marketers on your team, sharing what you've learned without being asked.

    What You Will Bring to the Role

    • Significant experience in B2B product marketing, ideally in enterprise software, with a track record of owning positioning and messaging end to end, not just contributing pieces of it.

    • A real competitive intelligence practice under your belt. You've built and maintained a program that sales relied on, not just responded to research requests as they came in.

    • Comfort marketing technical products to technical buyers. You can go deep enough into a technical concept to be credible with a developer, and simplify it enough to be clear to an executive.

    • Field enablement experience at scale. You've built programs that changed how a sales team talked about a product, and you know how to tell if it worked.

    • Strong cross-functional instincts. You know how to build trust with product and sales without relying on authority, and how to bring people along on a positioning decision rather than just announcing it.

    • Comfort using AI tools in your day to day work. This isn't a checkbox, it's part of how the role actually operates.

    • Fluent in French and English.

    Your wellbeing, our mission. Join a company shaping a healthier world.

    GET TO KNOW US

    At Wellhub we're revolutionizing workplace wellness. Our platform connects employees worldwide to the best partners for fitness, mindfulness, therapy, nutrition, and sleep—all in one simple subscription. Headquartered in NYC with team members in Europe, North America and South America, we're on a mission to make every company a wellness company.We believe work should be fulfilling, inspiring, and balanced. Here, you'll find a team that values wellbeing, collaboration, and different perspectives, where passion and creativity push boundaries to create real impact. Your contributions will help shape a healthier, more balanced world for you and millions of people globally. 

    Join us in redefining the future of wellbeing!

    THE OPPORTUNITY

    Partner Marketing exists to fuel the growth and success of Wellhub's global partner network of gyms, studios and wellness businesses. The Senior Manager, Partner Marketing (France & Benelux) leads Partner Marketing strategy and execution for these markets, as part of Wellhub's regional EU Partner Marketing team.

    This person will act as the regional Point of Contact (POC) for Partner Marketing in France and Benelux, owning the local Business-to- Partner value proposition, brand positioning, network growth and engagement and, fitness industry events, working closely with Partnerships, local and cross-functional Marketing, Wellbeing Engagement, Product Development and Revenue teams to align strategy and execution. Reporting to the Partner Marketing Director, EU, this role combines strategic ownership of the region with hands-on execution.

    This role directly impacts the growth and satisfaction of Wellhub's partner network in France and Benelux, contributing to the team's broader goals around partner network growth, partner engagement, and partner satisfaction (PSAT).

     

    YOUR IMPACT

    • Market-Specific Value Proposition: Develop and implement the local Business to Partner value proposition across all partner-facing materials and touchpoints for France and Benelux.
    • Brand Awareness & Positioning: Build Wellhub's presence and credibility within the regional fitness industry through relationships with industry associations/alliances, sponsorships, events, media/publications, and key opinion leaders (KOLs).

    Power electronics are the bottleneck on every next-generation UAS airframe we build: motor controllers, gate drivers, and DC-DC stages are what define flight time, payload, thermal envelope, and field reliability. We're looking for a senior IC to own the analog power chain end-to-end across our UXV platforms: from MOSFET commutation simulation through PCB layout to lab validation. You will be the technical reference on power electronics inside our Lausanne engineering hub, unblocking propulsion, airframe, and embedded teams in parallel as we scale from prototype cadence to multi-platform deployment.

    Responsibilities

    • Power Stage Architecture: Lead motor-controller and DC-DC topology across fixed-wing, multicopter, and hybrid UXV platforms. Translate mission constraints into power-chain specification.

    • MOSFET Commutation & Gate-Drive Design: Own the analog switching design: dead-time tuning, gate shaping, switching-loss vs EMI vs thermal trade-offs.

    • Multi-fidelity Simulation: Deploy the full stack: analytical loss budgeting, transient SPICE (LTspice), system-level modelling in PLECS or Simulink.

    • BLDC Drive Stages: Design three-phase inverters with integrated current sensing, protection, Trapezoidal and FOC-aware hardware interfaces.

    • EMI / EMC Engineering: Drive pre-compliance, filter design, and root-cause debug under flight-representative loads.

    • Prototype-to-Production: Take motor-controller PCBAs through revision discipline, DFM, and qualification - closing the loop on field returns.

    • Lab Validation: Execute bench characterization (power analysers, oscilloscopes, thermal imaging, double-pulse testing) and reconcile against simulation.

    • Firmware & Controls Interface: Partner with embedded and propulsion on FOC tuning, current-sense calibration, and the hardware/firmware compensation boundary.

    • Design Authority & Mentorship: Set the bar via design-decision records and reference designs. Mentor 1–2 junior engineers.

    • MSc or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Power Electronics, or equivalent.

    • 5+ years of hands-on R&D experience on motor drives, BLDC/PMSM controllers, or high-power-density power electronics.

    • Deep working mastery of MOSFET commutation design: gate-driver selection, dead-time tuning, switching transitions, loss budgets.

    • Proven ownership of at least one motor-controller PCBA shipped from prototype through production (or pre-production qualification): ideally on drone, robotics, eVTOL, or automotive platforms.

    • Fluency in simulation (LTspice, PLECS, or Simulink) and PCB design (Altium).

    • Lab-bench discipline: you've personally debugged what simulation missed.

    • Comfort with scale-up iteration speed and end-to-end ownership.

    • English fluent (working language); French is a nice-to-have, not a requirement.

    Bonus points for: GaN / SiC experience, safety-critical design exposure , applied control theory implemented in hardware, exposure to defense, aerospace, or UAS programmes.

    Senior Network Developer

    About Share

    Share is the global marketplace for bandwidth. We aggregate telco infrastructure across Africa (fiber routes, subsea capacity, data centers, cloud on-ramps) into a single intelligence layer. That lets ISPs, hyperscalers and AI companies get connectivity where they need it in seconds, not months.

We're replacing that with one neutral exchange: an API on top of real infrastructure, with prices set by actual supply and demand. It's already live across East Africa, with thousands of kilometers of fiber, 12 infrastructure providers, 10 data centers, and around 8 million people served.

    The Role

    Our network is the foundation of the product. Every route a customer provisions through our API has to exist, perform and stay up on real hardware. We're hiring a Senior Network Developer to design and build that network as software: a distributed, multi-provider fabric that engineers change through code, not by logging into devices.

    You'll own the network architecture end to end. That covers our BGP edge (transit, peering at KIXP and LINX, private interconnects with hyperscalers), the backbone, and the PoPs and data centers we're adding across the continent. You'll set the standards our network is built to, which partner ISPs connecting to us will inherit. As we grow, you'll also help build the network engineering team.

    What you'll do

    • Design the backbone and PoP architecture as standard, repeatable building blocks, from edge to data center, so we can add capacity and new markets without redesigning each time.

    • Drive our move to Segment Routing and a clean IP architecture, including IPv4 reuse, IPv6, and how customer and internal address space coexist.

    • Build on disaggregated white-box hardware (Edgecore with IP Infusion OcNOS today), and make the hardware and software calls that keep us fast and affordable.

    • Turn operations into software. That means a source of truth (Nautobot), templated config (Jinja), and CI/CD with validation, staged rollouts and rollback for every change.

    • Build the telemetry and observability that show what the network is really doing. Use AI where it actually helps: anomaly detection, automated triage, and auto-remediation with a human in the loop.

    • Own availability. Limit how much any failure can affect, mitigate first and diagnose second, and turn post-mortems into fixes in the system.

    • Work with our software team on the API and provisioning layer that exposes the network to customers, and with partner ISPs' engineers on the hand-off.

    • Help hire and develop the engineers who'll run this with you.

    Our Ideal Candidate

    • 8+ years building and operating large networks at a hyperscaler, CDN, internet exchange, carrier or ISP.

    • Deep BGP at scale: route policy, communities, RPKI, traffic engineering, peering and transit.

    • Strong data center and backbone design. You know Clos/EVPN-VXLAN fabrics and MPLS or Segment Routing, and when each makes sense.

    • Hands-on with white-box or disaggregated networking, including choosing hardware and knowing where the silicon limits you.

    • You treat the network as code. You write automation yourself (Python or similar), and you've built or run the pipelines, source of truth and telemetry that make that safe.

    • You've owned availability for something that couldn't go down, and can walk us through a real incident: what broke, how you found it, and what you changed.

    • You think like an owner. You bring ideas, not tickets, and you want to help build a team, not just a network.

    • A clear, direct communicator who's comfortable with partners' engineers and with our founders.

    • Experience at an internet exchange, or running peering at scale.

    • 400G/800G and optical (ZR) deployments, including vendor selection and certification.

    • Building networks in emerging markets such as Africa or Latin America.

    • DDoS mitigation at the edge.

    If you don't tick every box but have built and run large networks in production, apply anyway.

    Competitive salary and meaningful equity in a venture-backed company (US-incorporated, with a Kenya operating entity)

    Network Operations Engineer

    1. About the role

    Share is the global marketplace for bandwidth. We aggregate telco infrastructure into a single layer and give ISPs, hyperscalers, and AI companies a clean path to deliver connectivity into every home and business across Kenya and the continent. Behind that marketplace is a real network: a BGP edge peering with Tier 1 transit, hyperscalers, and local exchanges, an MPLS backbone, aggregation and access gear, and the systems that watch all of it.

    For the partners who run on us, the network is the product, and the NOC is where they feel it. A clean shift is a partner who never knew anything happened. That is the bar.

    We are early and the team is small, so we cannot afford a pair of hands that only knows how to escalate. We need a capable network engineer who can stand a shift, resolve real faults without waking anyone, and then keep building the network while East Africa sleeps: propagation and peering checks, health passes across the estate, config changes through to merge, tickets off the board, automation that takes the next repetitive job off everyone's plate. The watching is the floor of this role, not the ceiling.

    The NOC you would be joining is not a legacy one. We are building it as an AI assisted operations environment from the ground up. The forwarding plane runs on open source routing and forwarding software, every device configuration lives in Git, and an LLM layer sits on top of the live network state. When something moves, that layer reads the telemetry, correlates it against the topology and the config history, and puts a probable cause and a candidate fix in front of the engineer on shift. The point is not to replace your judgment. It is to collapse the time between an alert firing and you knowing where to look, so mean time to repair is measured in minutes.

    You sit inside that system. You use it, you push back on it when it is wrong, and what you catch that it misses is part of how it gets smarter. As we build automation out across the NOC, you are not just a consumer of the tooling. You help write it.

    2. What you'll do

    Watch, and know what you're looking at. Sit on our monitoring stack (Zabbix and Grafana dashboards, flow telemetry, alerting) and actually read it. Learn what normal looks like so abnormal jumps out at you: a BGP session that dropped, a link that went down, latency climbing on a path, a capacity threshold breached, a partner suddenly pushing or pulling nothing.

    Troubleshoot and resolve. This is where you earn your seat. Confirm the alert is real, gather the facts, and localise the fault: one peer or many, us or upstream, a real outage or a monitoring blip. The assistive layer surfaces a likely diagnosis and a suggested fix, the config history is right there in Git, and the runbooks are live. Your job is to read all of it critically, decide what is actually true, and close out what you can on your own. Every ticket you resolve yourself is one our senior people did not get pulled out of deep work, or out of bed, to deal with.

    Keep the network healthy, not just alive. A quiet shift is not an idle one. Run the proactive passes: check that routes are propagating the way they should, that RPKI and filter chains are doing their job, that peering and transit sessions are clean across the edge, that no PoP is drifting toward a capacity wall. Catch the slow degradations that never trip an alert. The day team should inherit a network in a known good state.

    Build and automate. The repetitive parts of this job should not stay repetitive. Write the scripts that turn a manual check into a scheduled one. Push our config automation forward (Jinja driven generation, NAPALM or NETCONF/gNMI against the devices) so changes ship from data, not from memory. When the assistive layer keeps missing the same thing, that is a candidate for automation, and you are well placed to build it during the hours nobody else is online.

    Move the work forward. You are part of the network team, working the same board they do. Pick up tickets from the Linear queue, take config changes through review to merge, and keep our source of truth (Nautobot) accurate as the estate changes. Real work lands while East Africa is offline, so the team wakes up further ahead than they went to bed.

    Report exactly what is happening. For everything you cannot or should not fix alone, the handoff has to be clean: what is wrong, where, since when, what is affected, whether it is getting worse, and what you have already tried. No guessing dressed up as fact. No "the internet is down." A clear, written incident note a senior engineer can act on the moment they open it, and a tidy handover to the East Africa team at the end of your shift.

    Escalate well. Know the ladder cold: what you are cleared to touch, what you must not touch alone, and who to bring in for what. Escalating early on a genuine outage is good judgment. Sitting silently on a problem because you were unsure is the one thing that gets people out of bed angry. Handle what you can, raise the rest fast and clearly, and do not turn either dial too far.

    3. Who we're looking for

    A network engineer who can stand on their own through a shift, and who treats the quiet hours as time to build rather than time to wait. You will not be the most senior engineer on this team, and you do not need to be. The people you escalate to are CCIE level. What we need from you is independence and range: work a problem properly, resolve a fair share of it yourself, and use what is left of the shift to actually move the network forward. Pair that with clear reporting, sound judgment about when to bring in help, and the instinct to question a machine's suggestion rather than follow it blindly, and you are who we are looking for.

    Must-have

    • Strong networking competence, held in your hands rather than on paper. CCNA and well beyond it. You understand TCP/IP, routing and switching, IP addressing and subnetting, DNS, DHCP, NAT, and how they behave when they go wrong.

    • Real troubleshooting instinct. Given a degraded link or a dropped session, you know where to look and what to rule out. You can read BGP session state, follow a path with ping and traceroute, and tell a local fault from an upstream one without waiting to be told.

    • Working BGP knowledge. Reading communities and route policy, spotting a flap or a leaky origin, understanding how transit, peering, and RPKI behave at the edge.

    • Comfortable on the gear and the CLI. Linux, network device CLIs, and dashboards are familiar ground. We run MikroTik (RouterOS) across the network and so do many partners, so RouterOS experience is a real plus.

    • Comfortable working with config in Git. Configuration lives in repos, not on devices. Reading a diff, understanding why a config changed, and proposing one yourself should not be foreign to you.

    • Some scripting, and the appetite to do more. Bash or Python, enough to automate the repetitive parts away and to grow into our config and automation pipelines. We are not hiring a button pusher.

    • Clear written English. You can describe a technical situation accurately and briefly so someone picking it up cold understands it instantly.

    • Calm under pressure and dependable. When the graphs go red you get more precise, not more panicked. You show up for every shift, alert and on time.

    • Located in New Zealand or a nearby time zone where covering our deep overnight maps onto your normal working day.

    Nice-to-have

    • CCNP, or MikroTik MTCNA / MTCRE.

    • Prior NOC, ISP, or carrier operations experience.

    • Hands on with MPLS (L3VPN, EVPN) and the multi-tenant isolation a shared backbone needs.

    • Exposure to open source and white box routing or forwarding stacks (SONiC, IP Infusion OcNOS, FRR, or similar).

    • Network source of truth and automation tooling (Nautobot, NAPALM, Jinja config generation, NETCONF or gNMI).

    • Familiarity with a monitoring stack such as Zabbix, Grafana, Loki, or Prometheus, and with flow telemetry.

    • Working familiarity with FreeRADIUS, CoA and Disconnect flows, and how session control and accounting hook into the network.

    • Exposure to applying ML or AI in network operations: anomaly detection, predictive failure analysis, automated triage or remediation.

    • IPv6 and dual stack exposure, and internet exchange operations (looking glass and route server behaviour, IRR and RPKI hygiene).

    4. What we offer

    • A seat inside a serious, very senior network team, with people who have deep service provider backgrounds and will sharpen you fast. You will see how a real carrier network behaves under live conditions.

    • A front row seat to how a network actually gets run in 2026. Open source forwarding, config as code, and an LLM layer doing real operational work. Not a slide about the future of network operations, but the environment you would work in every shift, and help build.

    • Real engineering, not just monitoring. The role is built so the quiet hours go into automation, propagation and health work, and tickets off the board. The path into deeper network engineering and automation work is the plan, not a vague someday.

    • Competitive salary and private health and wellness benefits, fully remote, in a mission driven, investor backed company building the backbone of Africa's next generation internet.

Your tasks

  • Get CAD ready for rendering: Turn heavy mechanical assemblies from engineering into clean 3D assets that render, animate and run in real time without falling apart. The hardware stands in our workshop, and the next machine is never far behind.
  • Show what is inside: Exploded views, cutaways and assembly animations that explain the mechanics without a technical drawing, so customers understand the tech behind the product.
  • Materials that look real: Build shaders for aluminum, stainless steel, glass, rubber, carbon, plastics, displays and LEDs, so a render reads as the actual object rather than as a render. Scenes, materials and rigs stay organized, so the next project does not start from zero.
  • Motion design in a house style: Titles, typography, transitions, logo animation, and 2D animation for interface elements like animated displays and icons. It should look like us, not like a template pack.
  • Editing and post: Footage from the workshop and tests, mixed with 3D work, becomes what we use on the website, on social, at trade shows and in investor meetings. Editing, grading, sound, subtitles, and a version that fits each channel.
  • Put AI to work: You use AI and generative tools (e.g. comfy) where they actually save time, whether that is concepting, cleanup or upscaling. You keep testing what is new, keep what earns a place in the pipeline, and drop the rest.

Your profile

  • Background: A degree in motion design, animation or media design, or a self taught route with a reel that makes the question pointless.
  • Experience: At least two years of hands on work, whether from an internship, freelance jobs, a studio or your own projects. What the work looks like matters more to us than where it was made.
  • CAD is not new to you: You have opened engineering data before and know roughly what happens when a heavy assembly meets a render engine.
  • Reel: Hard surfaces, metal, glass and light. Even one personal project done properly tells us more than ten client jobs you only assisted on.
  • Tools: Experience in Blender and Cinema 4D, Octane is a plus. After Effects and either Premiere for the cut.
  • How you work: Hands on and fast to a first version. You get things finished instead of perfect, and you notice when a detail stops being worth the hours.
  • Languages: Fluent English. Good German is a real plus.

Why us?

  • Your work is what people see of us: Almost everything the outside world sees of our robots comes out of your hands, and you decide how that looks.
  • Everything under one roof: Labs, workshop and test rigs are in the same Kreuzberg building. The engineer you need is a walk away, not a ticket.
  • Room to get better: Paid learning time and a personal budget for it, projects where something is allowed to not work the first time, and support for portfolio work and conference talks as the company becomes known.
  • Benefits: A benefits package you put together yourself, covering mobility, home setup, health or food. Plus one extra paid day off a year for volunteering or a project you care about.

Send us a link to your work. Best case it includes something you took from CAD data to a finished render, with a note on how. Skip the cover letter.

Process: Intro call -> Portfolio deep-dive -> Half-day on-site visit with a small design exercise -> Offer.

We build robots for everyone, so we want a team that reflects that. We hire on what you can do, and we welcome applications from people who are underrepresented in 3D and motion. If you don't tick every box but think this is your job, apply anyway.

As agentic AI accelerates, Parloans are shaping the foundation of a new era in customer experience, one where customer support is no longer transactions, but meaningful exchanges. It is not just a vision; Parloa has powered over ONE BILLION interactions between global enterprise brands and their customers, with companies like <a href="http://booking.com">Booking.com</a>, HealthEquity, Allianz, SAP, BarmeniaGothaer, and TUI already deploying Parloa at scale.</p> <h2><strong>About the role:</strong></h2> <p>As a <strong>Staff Product Engineer</strong>, you will work directly inside our most strategic enterprise customers. You will build the software that makes their AI agents work in production, and be measured by the difference it makes for the customer.</p> <p>Our agents are built by business users in Parloa’s platform, AMP. AMP already comes with a broad library of tools and integrations. Your job is the part AMP does not cover yet for a given customer: the last connection into their systems, or a capability the product does not have. Our customers are large enterprises in financial services, telecom, insurance, travel and retail. For them, a working prototype is where an engagement starts, not where it ends.</p> <p>The work comes in two forms. Some engagements run for years. You stay with the account, deepen its integrations and help it grow into new use cases. Others are short experiments. You test a new idea with a real customer and decide quickly whether it is worth building. At Staff level, you take on the hardest cases of both: accounts where a pilot-grade solution would fail in production, and capabilities nobody at Parloa has built before. Staff means harder problems and more ambiguity, not less hands-on work.</p> <p>On many accounts, you work alongside a Deployment Strategist. Think of the two of you as the account’s leadership team. The Deployment Strategist acts as its CPO and defines what success looks like. You act as its CTO and own the architecture and the build. On accounts without a Deployment Strategist, you own the engineering yourself.</p> <h2><strong>Areas of ownership:</strong></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Lead the hardest engagements.</strong> Run complex programmes with several workstreams. Make the architecture decisions that span Parloa’s platform and several parts of the customer’s organization.</li> <li><strong>Build what AMP does not cover yet.</strong> Systems of record, telephony and contact-center integrations, state management, data readiness, multi-agent orchestration and retrieval. When the answer is unclear, build a prototype quickly and decide whether it is worth pursuing before Parloa invests a full quarter in it.</li> <li><strong>Own production quality and security.</strong> Evals, production readiness, observability and incident playbooks for enterprise-scale traffic. Meet the data handling standards a regulated customer expects, including PII, access control and audit trails. Debug live issues, whether they are technical or caused by model behaviour.</li> <li><strong>Grow the account, and share what belongs in the product.</strong> Drive the second use case, the second business unit, the renewal. Set the delivery standard for other engineers on complex accounts. When something you build would help every customer, flag it. That is how Parloa decides what goes into the core product.</li> <li><strong>Mentor other Product Engineers</strong>, and take part in interviewing and hiring.</li> <li><strong>Use AI well, and set the standard for it.</strong> Decide how AI-assisted work is validated before it reaches a customer’s production traffic.</li> <li><strong>Represent Parloa with senior technical stakeholders.</strong> Work directly with the customer’s principal engineers, architects and security leaders. We are committed to building diverse and inclusive teams. Relation is offering a unique opportunity for an experienced Associate Director in Alliance Management to ensure that our strategic pharma partnerships continue to thrive and deliver.   • Manage the health and effectiveness of strategic pharma partnerships, building trusted relationships across Relation and partner organisations and influencing cross-functional stakeholders at all levels to maintain alignment and momentum.

  • Shape new partnerships from diligence through launch, collaborating closely with Growth, Corporate and Business Development to embed effective governance, contractual clarity and practical ways of working from the outset.

  • Raise the standard of partnering at Relation, applying learning across collaborations to strengthen governance, alliance management and organisational partnering capability as Relation’s portfolio grows.

  • A university degree in a relevant scientific or technical field, or equivalent experience.

  • Deep expertise working with complex collaboration agreements, with the judgement to interpret contractual commitments, identify implications and risks, and translate them into clear actions or governance decisions.

  • Experience working in data-rich, technology-enabled or AI/ML-enabled R&D environments is key, particularly in partnerships involving contractual alignment at the intersection of data, technology and intellectual property.

  • Strong scientific and drug discovery fluency, enabling you to operate credibly with senior scientific leaders and interdisciplinary teams.

  • A track record of influencing senior stakeholders without formal authority, navigating organisational complexity and building alignment across companies, disciplines and competing priorities.

  • Strong governance judgement, with experience bringing complex scientific, commercial, contractual and relational issues to senior decision-making forums.

  • Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to distill complexity into clear, decision-ready recommendations for senior leaders and external partners.

  • Confidence navigating disagreement, ambiguity and sensitive partner issues with diplomacy, sound judgement and integrity.

  • The ability to maintain strategic perspective and forward visibility while overseeing multiple complex partnerships in a fast-moving environment.

    Company Description

    We’re Checkout.com. You might not know our name, but companies like eBay, Spotify, Klarna, Uber, and Sony do, because we’re behind many of the digital experiences you use every day.


    We are where the world checks out, enabling over 10 billion transactions yearly for more than one billion global shoppers.

    Whether you want to book a holiday, order food, renew a subscription, or check out online, there’s a good chance our tech powers the payments behind the scenes. Our platform helps the most ambitious businesses deliver effortless digital experiences, at scale.

    If you want to do career-defining work, you’ve come to the right place. We move fast, think globally, and believe great teams are built by hiring exceptional people with conviction, curiosity, and the desire to make an impact.

    With 20 offices across six continents and London as our HQ, we’re shaping the future of fintech – and we’re just getting started.

    The role

    Checkout.com is looking for an enthusiastic Engineer I to join Finance Technology with a focus on Workday Adaptive Planning. Adaptive Planning supports finance, workforce, sales, and operational planning, giving teams a shared platform for budgeting, forecasting, modelling, reporting, and decision-making.

    This is an early-career engineering role for someone who wants to build depth in finance systems, application configuration, data integration, and operational support. You will work with Finance, Finance Technology, Data, and wider Corporate Technology teams to keep planning processes reliable, well-controlled, and easy to operate.

    You will have support from more senior engineers for complex design decisions, but you will be expected to work independently for longer periods on well-defined configuration, integration, support, and continuous-improvement tasks. This reflects Checkout’s Engineer 1 expectations: delivering small-to-medium-sized work, supporting common operational flows, communicating clearly, and taking ownership of the quality of what you deliver.

    How you’ll make an impact

    • Configure, maintain, and enhance Adaptive Planning models, dimensions, versions, levels, accounts, sheets, reports, dashboards, and planning workflows under appropriate guidance.

    • Support the delivery of budgeting, forecasting, headcount planning, scenario modelling, and management reporting capabilities for Finance and business stakeholders.

    • Build and support data loads and integrations between Adaptive Planning, Workday Financials, Workday HCM, and other approved internal or third-party systems.

    • Maintain data mappings, transformation rules, validation checks, and reconciliation processes so that planning data is complete, accurate, and traceable.

    • Monitor scheduled loads and integration tasks, investigate failures, and resolve common data or configuration issues within agreed service levels.

    • Triage incidents and service requests, identifying root causes and escalating complex or high-risk issues with clear evidence and recommended next steps.

    • Partner with Finance stakeholders to understand requirements and translate them into maintainable system configuration, reporting, or integration changes.

    • Contribute to the assessment and delivery of future analytics data flows, including the potential use of Adaptive Planning data in BigQuery and management analytics.

    • Participate in testing, regression testing, release preparation, and controlled deployment of Adaptive Planning changes.

    • Follow change-control, access-management, data-quality, and audit requirements relevant to financial systems and planning data.

    • Create clear documentation, support guides, data dictionaries, integration runbooks, and knowledge-base articles so that operational knowledge is shared rather than held by one person.

    • Identify recurring manual work or failure patterns and propose practical automation and process improvements.

    What we’re looking for

    Essential experience and skills

    • Experience in a finance systems, enterprise applications, data, reporting, or integration environment.

    • Practical experience with Workday Adaptive Planning, or strong experience with a comparable planning, performance-management, ERP, or finance application and a clear ability to learn Adaptive quickly.

    • Understanding of core finance planning concepts such as budgets, forecasts, actuals, variance analysis, allocations, dimensions, hierarchies, and scenarios.

    • Experience configuring or supporting structured data models, application workflows, reports, dashboards, or business rules.

    • Ability to work with data imports, exports, mappings, transformations, validations, and reconciliations.

    • Strong troubleshooting skills, with the ability to break down an issue, gather evidence, identify likely causes, and communicate findings clearly.

    • Good attention to detail and an understanding of why accuracy, access control, auditability, and repeatability matter in finance systems.

    • Ability to manage small-to-medium-sized tasks independently while knowing when to ask for help or escalate.

    • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work effectively with Finance and Technology stakeholders.

    Desirable experience

    • Workday Adaptive Planning certification or implementation experience.

    • Experience with Adaptive Planning Integration, Planning Data Loader, APIs, or equivalent enterprise planning integration tooling.

    • Experience integrating planning systems with Workday Financials, Workday HCM, an ERP, a data warehouse, or a reporting platform.

    • Familiarity with SOX controls, financial audit requirements, data privacy, and segregation of duties.

    • Experience supporting month-end, budget, forecast, or management-reporting cycles.

    • Exposure to Agile delivery, ticket-driven change management, incident management, or service-management practices.

    What success looks like

    After the first 6–12 months, you will be able to:

    • Support common Adaptive Planning configuration, data-load, and reporting requests with limited supervision.

    • Diagnose and resolve routine integration or data-quality issues using a structured troubleshooting approach.

    • Deliver small-to-medium-sized enhancements from requirement clarification through testing, documentation, and controlled release.

    • Explain key planning data flows, mappings, dependencies, and operational controls to Finance and Technology colleagues.

    • Improve the reliability or efficiency of at least one recurring planning or finance-technology process.

    • Maintain accurate, useful documentation and contribute positively to team ceremonies, reviews, and knowledge-sharing sessions.

    Working style and behaviours

    We are looking for someone who:

    • Takes ownership of tasks and follows through on commitments.

    • Acts with urgency and accountability when issues affect Finance or business reporting.

    • Is curious about how finance processes, data, and technology fit together.

    • Communicates clearly, especially when explaining risk, blockers, trade-offs, or support impact.

    • Welcomes feedback and actively develops their technical and domain knowledge.

    • Collaborates generously and shares knowledge so the team does not depend on a single subject-matter expert.

    • Looks for durable automation and simpler operating processes rather than repeatedly working around the same manual problem.

    Why join Finance Technology?

    You will work on systems that sit at the centre of how Checkout.com plans, forecasts, reports, and makes financial decisions. The role offers the opportunity to develop a broad foundation across enterprise applications, finance processes, integrations, data quality, controls, and automation while working closely with experienced Finance and Technology professionals.

    Additional Information

    Bring all of you to work

    The sea is the physical layer of the economy: our energy, data and trade move across it and under it. It is also Europe's most exposed flank. Cheap underwater drones, divers and mines now threaten ports, naval bases, subsea cables and offshore energy sites, and most of what is funded today stops at detection: it tells you a drone has entered the harbour, not how to stop it before it reaches the hull or the cable.

    Pelagon is creating the category of maritime interdiction: detection and action together. We design, deploy and operate protection zones around critical maritime infrastructure: a persistent sensing network running our own acoustic-first AI detects and classifies threats, and an underwater interceptor acts on them.

    We sell to navies and coast guards, and to the civilian operators of ports, subsea cables and offshore energy.

    Pelagon was founded by Aymeric de Pontbriand (serial deeptech entrepreneur, founded and exited Scortex) and Gauthier Bouxin (French Navy officer, then McKinsey).     • Open our priority export markets: the Baltic and the Nordics, the Black Sea, the Gulf and Southeast Asia.

    • Define process windows, recipes, operating conditions and acceptance criteria. 
    • Use structured experimentation, including Design of Experiments (DoE) where appropriate, to understand process sensitivities and optimize performance. 
    • Improve process repeatability, reproducibility, robustness and within-wafer / wafer-to-wafer homogeneity. 
    • Prepare processes and equipment for increasing wafer sizes, batch sizes and production volumes.

    • Act as a key technical interface between Advanced R&D and Production. 
    • Convert R&D process building blocks into stable, documented and manufacturable processes. 
    • Assess manufacturability, scalability and process risks before transfer to production.

    • Lead or contribute to Process Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (PFMEA) for critical fabrication steps, identifying potential failure modes, their effects on device performance and appropriate prevention and control measures.

    • Monitor and improve production process performance, yield and throughput.

    • Define and maintain relevant process KPIs and contribute to continuous-improvement initiatives. 
    • Promote best practices that increase process stability, repeatability and equipment utilization.

    • Provide hands-on technical support to cleanroom operators and production teams. 
    • Support equipment qualification, troubleshooting and process recovery following equipment interventions. 
    • Work closely with equipment suppliers and internal teams to resolve technical issues. 
    • Contribute to a safe, disciplined and efficient cleanroom environment.

    • Search and analyze scientific and technical literature to support process development and troubleshooting.

    About Nabla

    We are a team of entrepreneurs, clinicians and engineers committed to bringing back joy to the practice of medicine.

    Together with a community of clinician innovators, we’ve harnessed the best of machine learning science to develop Nabla: the leading AI assistant that’s restoring the human connection at the heart of healthcare.     Backed by a recent $70M Series C, we’re hiring to build the next generation of clinical AI and improve the lives of clinicians and patients everywhere.

    Led by former Meta AI Research engineers, our team has consistently anticipated how AI can revolutionize healthcare delivery. Our Machine Learning team continually leverages the latest advancements to unlock AI’s full potential in healthcare.

    Yann LeCun, Meta’s ex-Chief AI Scientist and Turing award winner, is an advisor to Nabla. He’s now focused on AMI Labs, with whom we have a close partnership.

    Engineering at Nabla

    Engineering at Nabla is lean, fast-moving, and deeply technical. Our teams span machine learning, native desktop applications, and platform infrastructure to deliver AI into clinical settings reliably and at scale.

    Your Team

    At Nabla, product development is led jointly by Engineering and Product, and organized into cross-functional squads, each focused on a specific product area. Squads bring together product managers, designers, engineers of different profiles, and domain experts, and operate with a high level of ownership.

    As an AI Engineer, you’ll join one of these squads and contribute end to end to a specific part of the product.

    What you'll do

    As an AI/ML Software Engineer, you’ll play a key role in redefining clinicians’ workflows, unlocking better care for patients, and ensuring Nabla remains at the forefront of AI innovation. You will take ownership of high-impact projects and contribute to the growth and maturity of our engineering team and product.

    Within a team of experts who have built large-scale production systems at Meta, Google, and Microsoft, you will:

    • Build agentic pipelines: chains of LLM-based agents that work together on complex clinical documentation tasks.

    • Go beyond ambient scribing to fully redefine clinicians’ workflows with AI, unlocking transformative efficiencies and improved patient care.

    • Integrate LLM provider APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and others) into production features.

    • Design prompts and build evaluation frameworks to measure and improve output quality, then iterate quickly based on results.

    • Write clean, production-grade code and own your features end to end, from design to deployment and monitoring in a live healthcare setting.

    • Work closely with product managers to turn model capabilities into reliable, scalable product features.

    To get a sense of the impact you’ll have:

    • Nabla processes 300 billion tokens/month with LLMs.

    • By the time you’ve read this posting, Nabla will have transcribed 100 new hours of live audio and generated 500 new clinical notes, saving 125 hours of doctor time.

    Your DNA:

    The ideal candidate will bring strong software engineering skills and a practical, hands-on approach to building with LLMs.

    • You have 3+ years writing production code, with solid skills in software design, testing, and system architecture.

    • You’re proficient in one or more widely used back-end languages (Java, Kotlin, C++, Go, etc.).

    • You’ve built features or products using LLM provider APIs, including prompting and evaluation. You don’t need to have trained or fine-tuned models yourself.

    • You can turn a fuzzy product requirement into a working, testable pipeline.

    • You have a passion for going beyond the status quo to redefine workflows and unlock better care for patients.

    • You communicate clearly and effectively.

    • Bonus: Experience building multi-agent systems or agent orchestration frameworks is a strong plus.

    Our Stack

    • Kotlin for backend services

    • LLM provider APIs (OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, and others) for the models themselves

    • Agent orchestration frameworks for building chains of agents

    • Prompt evaluation and testing tools to track output quality over time

    • Google Cloud & Kubernetes for deployment

    Our offices are based in Paris 3e (Arts & Métiers).
    Remote policy: 1-2 days a week (with some flexibility). Possibility of working remotely 1-2 weeks once a year.

    • Stock ownership

    • 100% healthcare coverage

    • Meal vouchers

    • Public transportation costs covered at 50%

    • Exercise class during the workday: Yoga, running, pilates, HIIT

    • Unlimited budget for book purchases, so you can continue to learn about ML / Healthcare

We consistently look for ways to improve and do not shy away from doing the work to excel.
